description: Returns what happened in software after a given date, so an agent can patch the gap between its training data and today: packages among the most popular on npm, PyPI, crates.io and Packagist that shipped a NEW MAJOR VERSION after the date (with the version that existed at that date, the new majors and their first release dates, the latest version, and an upgrade-guide link when one exists), runtimes, frameworks and platforms released or ended since (Python, Node.js, PHP, Java, Django, Laravel, Ubuntu, PostgreSQL and about 35 more), runtimes ending within 180 days, and AI models released since by the main providers with their prices. Read-only and requires no authentication. Results are computed from registry publication dates and cached for an hour. Coverage is the most popular packages (not every package), 0.x-to-0.y changes and calendar-versioned packages are not reported as major versions, and deprecations that happened before Vigia started tracking are not listed. Use it once at the start of a coding session, passing the month your training data ends, or when you suspect a library you know has changed a lot. To dig into one package use upgrade_impact (npm) or package_status; for one runtime use eol_status.

cutoff.description: The month or date your training data ends, as YYYY-MM (the last day of that month is used) or YYYY-MM-DD, for example "2025-06". It must be a past date after 2015

ecosystems.description: Restrict the package list to these ecosystems; omit for all four

limit.description: Maximum number of packages in new_major_versions, most popular first, from 1 to 100 (default 30)

name: changes_since_cutoff
title: What changed since my knowledge cutoff
